newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Linotype sees profits within two years.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Linotype sees profits within two years.

text.p: German printing machinery group Linotype-Hell AG on Tuesday repeated it was confident of being back in the black two years from now, with the help of its new majority owner, Heidelberger Druck.
The company, which also confirmed a 152.7 million mark ($89.4 million) group loss for 1996, said it had begun an intensive restructuring plan to reduce its costs.

"Once the repositioning of Linotype-Hell is complete and with the synergy effects of the planned merger with Heidelberger Druckmaschinen AG, Linotype-Hell expects to return to profit again within two years," the group said in a statement.
Linotype-Hell's loss position last year was capped by a 125 million-mark injection from Heidelberger Druckmaschinen, which made a successful bid for the company last year.
The injection must be repaid as soon as the profit position allows, Linotype-Hell said.

The group said it had reached agreement with works councils in Eschborn and Kiel over the restructuring plans, allowing it to go ahead with its project to concentrate the bulk of its activities in Kiel this year.
Linotype also released final sales and orders data for 1996, having already released preliminary figures in March.
Group sales dropped to 821.6 million marks from 860.6 million, amid continued structural changes in the printing industry and a "perceptible reluctance to buy on the client side."
Incoming orders dropped to 814.3 million marks from 866.5 million in the period.
"The economic problems that resulted brought Linotype-Hell to the brink of its existence," the statement said.
